correctness.rationale: The synchronous threshold-four rule on either six-regular graph deletes precisely the inactive vertices of residual degree at most two. A nonempty induced minimum-degree-three subset can never peel; if peeling stalls, its nonempty residual is such a subset. Successful seeds are an up-set, so all single deletions failing is necessary and sufficient for inclusion-minimality. An independent exact reproduction enumerated all 65,536 masks on each graph, finding nonpercolation by enumerating minimum-degree-three subsets and propagating containment, and cross-checking every mask by a FIFO activation-time recurrence. Shrikhande yields (6,3):96, (6,4):336, (6,5):1152, (6,6):576, (7,3):64, total 2224; the rook graph yields (6,3):288, (6,5):576, total 864. No others occur. Exact degree-signature and seven-set comparisons reproduce both claims, including the witness activation layers. Independent adjacency-preserving permutation enumeration returns 192 Shrikhande automorphisms and the same 64-set orbit. The twelve linear maps in the frozen certificate are invertible because their images contain the generating difference set; their translations therefore give 192 distinct automorphisms, so the reproduced orbit is also their affine orbit. Degree six and common-neighbor count two give the same adjacency spectrum (6, 2, -2 with multiplicities 1, 6, 9); rook neighborhoods are two disjoint triangles, whereas Shrikhande neighborhoods are cycles of length six. Replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/graph_census.py. Both frozen checkers were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: This natural strongly regular graph pair has matching parameters and spectrum, and even matches on minimum contagious cardinality at this threshold. The upper size of an inclusion-minimal contagious set is nevertheless different; the exact completion-time census and a complete affine-orbit characterization identify precisely how. This gives a concrete invariant and a reusable benchmark for finite bootstrap or core-deletion arguments, not merely another computation of the known rook minimum.
